title: Dynamics
intro: How quantum states change in time: the Schrödinger equation and its solution $e^{-iHt}$, what a Hamiltonian does to a qubit, the Heisenberg picture in which observables move instead of states, conserved quantities, and the harmonic oscillator.

blocks.text: A quantum reservoir is a system left to evolve under a fixed Hamiltonian between inputs. Everything about how it mixes information, how fast, and what it can never forget is a question about that Hamiltonian. This topic gives the tools to answer such questions.

items: The Schrödinger Equation (#/quantum/dynamics/schrodinger-equation): the equation of motion, energy eigenstates, precession of a spin in a field, and Rabi oscillation.

Symmetries and Conservation (#/quantum/dynamics/symmetries-and-conservation): the Heisenberg picture, why an operator that commutes with $H$ is conserved, and the parity symmetry of the reservoir Hamiltonian.
The Harmonic Oscillator (#/quantum/dynamics/harmonic-oscillator): ladder operators, Fock states, coherent states and quadratures, the language of continuous-variable reservoirs.

blocks.text: Time evolution here is always unitary, so it never forgets anything: distances between states are preserved exactly. The QRC shelf's whole treatment of fading memory starts from adding something non-unitary to these dynamics (The Echo State Property (#/qrc/foundations/echo-state-property)).

items: J. J. Sakurai and J. Napolitano, Modern Quantum Mechanics, 3rd edition, Cambridge University Press (2020), chapter 2
D. J. Griffiths and D. F. Schroeter, Introduction to Quantum Mechanics, 3rd edition, Cambridge University Press (2018), chapters 2 and 4
